Team —

Following the infra intake from Acme, they want a recommendation for how their VPC will connect to a Redwood Private deployment. Acme is very strict on traffic egress controls and requires that all management/control-plane calls terminate over a private path not exposed to the public internet.

Goal: produce a concise recommendation (<=1 page) with tradeoffs and a risk/mitigation table by EOD Dec 1. I attached a skeleton "latency-cost-table.xlsx" and a placeholder diagram (s2s-diagram.png) to ground the discussion.

Quick context:
- Customer: Acme Health (HIPAA, regional data residency requirement)
- Desired: Up to 1.5k rps for short-lived inference requests; burst to 4k rps across multiple regions
- Constraint: Acme will not allow cross-account VPC peering that requires route table exposure to their central network team without a managed gateway option

Initial asks:
1) Quick summary of security posture for each connectivity option (VPC Peering, PrivateLink, Site-to-Site VPN)
2) Operational lift and SLA implications (what fails open/closed, monitoring hooks)
3) Ballpark monthly cost delta for expected throughput — use the attached sheet

Karthik/Marcus: please add kernel/throughput comments (peering vs interface endpoints). Laura: call out procurement and firewall/contract considerations. Julia: I copied you so Acme can confirm constraints — please add any must-haves.

Thanks —

Hannah —

High-level technical notes:

VPC Peering:
- Security: Simple L3 peering; traffic is private and does not traverse the public internet.
- Pros: Low latency, predictable bandwidth, no per-flow proxies. Good for heavy steady-state traffic.
- Cons: Cross-account peering requires careful route table management; not supported across regions without transit or peering mesh. Can expose subnet ranges if customer is conservative.

AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints):
- Security: App-layer-proxied; customer does not need to modify route tables or expose subnets. Endpoint ENIs are in the customer's VPC and traffic flows over AWS private backbone.
- Pros: Great for cross-account isolation and controlled exposure; per-connection security at the ENI level and simpler IAM-based access control.
- Cons: Performance: each endpoint has ENI-level throughput limits; costs scale with endpoint hours and Data Processing charges. For 4k rps bursts with large payloads, we need to evaluate quota and ENI scaling.

Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec):
- Security: Encrypted IPSec tunnels; can terminate on a customer gateway appliance or Transit Gateway.
- Pros: Works for customers that forbid peering or endpoints in their accounts; supports on-prem.
- Cons: Higher latency, potential jitter; scaling requires multiple tunnels or a managed VPN appliance (Transit Gateway with VPN or Direct Connect). Operationally heavier and may impact SLA.

Marcus and I will run a quick perf check against interface endpoints (small PoC) and update the latency/cost sheet.

Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer

Thanks everyone — summary below and asks for next steps. This will be the one-page recommendation that goes to the customer and Legal.

Summary (decision inputs):
- VPC Peering: ruled out for Acme due to cross-account route exposure policy. Note: keep documented as an option for customers willing to accept cross-account peering (best latencies).
- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): preferred for cross-account isolation and simplest operational model for Acme's cloud VPCs, provided Acme will own the endpoints. Tradeoffs: per-endpoint throughput limits require us to provision multiple endpoints and use client-side connection pooling; costs include endpoint hours + data processing.
- Site-to-Site VPN: recommended for on-prem and hybrid customers. Works with Acme's FortiGate, but expect higher latency/jitter and additional ops for tunnel failover. Use Transit Gateway or managed VPN appliance for scale if they need steady bursts to 4k rps.

Risk & mitigations:
- Throughput: run quick PrivateLink perf PoC (Karthik/Marcus) to validate ENI scaling and measure p95 latency. If PrivateLink can't meet bursts, propose Transit Gateway + S2S for burst path.
- Management plane exposure: ensure all control-plane/backplane calls (model downloads, KV cache syncs) are forced over the PrivateLink or S2S path; no public egress. I will attach a management-plane diagram for Legal.
- Cost: Laura to produce TCO with line items for endpoint hours vs VPN appliance + Transit Gateway.

Action items: 
- Karthik/Marcus: PoC PrivateLink perf + p95 numbers by Fri Dec 4. (Karthik to update latency-cost-table.xlsx)
- Laura: draft procurement note and sample ACLs by Mon Dec 6.
- Hannah: final one-pager and management-plane diagram for Legal by Tue Dec 7.

Attachments referenced: latency-cost-table.xlsx, s2s-diagram.png, private-link-checklist.pdf

If Acme confirms they will own endpoints, PrivateLink is the default recommendation for cloud VPCs; S2S for on-prem. We'll present this as the modal path in the deployment runbook.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
